crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Brain Computer Interfaces
children.blurb: Brain computer interfaces are systems that read electrical or chemical signals from the nervous system and translate them into commands for a computer, a prosthetic, or a communication aid, and in some designs write information back into the brain through stimulation.

children.name: Early Signals of Dementia
children.blurb: Early signals of dementia refers to computational detection of subtle cognitive, behavioral, motor, or biomarker changes that may precede a clinical diagnosis.

children.name: Functional MRI Interpretation
children.blurb: Functional MRI interpretation uses AI to map brain activity from blood-oxygen-level-dependent signals, identify activation patterns tied to tasks or resting states, and support localization of language, motor, and memory functions before surgery.

children.name: Seizure Prediction
children.blurb: Seizure prediction is the use of machine learning to estimate the likelihood that a person with epilepsy will have a seizure within a short upcoming window, usually minutes to hours, based on physiological signals.

children.name: Cognitive Rehabilitation
children.blurb: Cognitive rehabilitation in this context covers AI systems that assess, train, and support recovery of cognitive functions such as attention, memory, executive function, and language after stroke, traumatic brain injury, or in neurodegenerative conditions.

sections.body: This field applies machine learning to data from the nervous system, from implanted electrodes to brain scans and behavioral logs. AI is now decoding intended hand movements for people with paralysis in research settings, flagging subtle speech and typing changes that may precede a dementia diagnosis, and reconstructing what a person sees or hears from functional MRI activity. It is also learning to recognize pre-seizure patterns in electroencephalography and to adjust memory or attention exercises in cognitive rehabilitation software. These are working systems in clinical trials and specialized clinics, not just laboratory demos. The work is narrow, each model handles one signal or one task.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has real but uneven progress. Seizure prediction has moved from chance level to useful warning times in some patients, though false alarms remain common. Brain computer interfaces can type at modest speeds for a few users, but they require surgery and daily calibration. Dementia signal models perform well on curated research data, yet they often fail when applied to routine clinic notes or diverse populations. Functional MRI interpretation can map language and motor areas, but it is not a mind reader and its results vary with scanner and task. Across this site's 1000 medical AI models, only a small fraction are cleared for routine neuro care, and most remain research tools because brain data is noisy, personal, and hard to label.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for hardware and direct neural control should start with Brain Computer Interfaces, which explains implants, signal decoding, and what users can currently do. Early Signals of Dementia covers the behavioral and speech markers that models look for before a formal diagnosis, useful for understanding screening tools. Functional MRI Interpretation shows how AI turns brain activity into maps of language, vision, and memory, and where that mapping breaks down. Seizure Prediction focuses on electroencephalography and the challenge of warning someone without crying wolf. Cognitive Rehabilitation ties the section together by showing how these signals can feed adaptive training programs after stroke or injury. Together the pages move from reading the brain to acting on what is read.
